Assign exposures to people over their own time windows

Source: R/expose.R
svy_expose.Rd

For each person, averages an exposure around their home location over one or more time windows measured from an anchor date, and reports how much of each window had data. It works the same way for rasters, monitor readings, gridded tables and area-level tables (see svy_exposure()).

Usage

svy_expose(
  data,
  exposure,
  windows = svy_windows("prenatal_postnatal"),
  radius_km = 5,
  window_unit = c("days", "weeks", "months", "years"),
  id = "id",
  date = "date",
  lon = "lon",
  lat = "lat",
  date_is = c("anchor", "interview"),
  age_months = NULL,
  assign = c("mean", "nearest", "idw"),
  idw_power = 2,
  fun = c("mean", "median", "max", "min"),
  min_coverage = 0.75,
  min_sources = 1,
  area = NULL,
  urban = "urban",
  name = "exposure",
  format = c("long", "wide")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (or sf points) with one row per person, with columns for identifier, date and, unless exposure is area-level, longitude and latitude.

exposure

An exposure source from svy_exposure(), or anything svy_exposure() accepts (a raster, a data frame, a file path).

windows

A named list of c(start, end) offsets, or a preset from svy_windows().

radius_km

Buffer radius or radii in kilometres, for example c(1, 2, 5). Use "dhs" for the DHS displacement rule (2 km urban, 5 km rural), which needs a column named urban (TRUE/FALSE, the DHS codes 1/2, or "urban"/"rural").

window_unit

Unit of the window offsets: "days" (default), "weeks", "months" or "years".

id, date, lon, lat

Column names in data.

date_is

"anchor" if date is already the date windows are measured from, for example date of birth. "interview" if date is the interview or measurement date and the anchor is the date of birth derived as date - age_months.

age_months

Column with the child's age in months; needed when date_is = "interview".

assign

For monitor and grid sources: "mean" of monitors within the radius, "nearest" monitor within the radius, or "idw" (inverse-distance weighted mean).

idw_power

Distance exponent for "idw".

fun

For rasters: how to summarise cells in the buffer, "mean", "median", "max" or "min".

min_coverage

Minimum share (0 to 1) of window days that must have data. Default 0.75.

min_sources

For monitor and grid sources: minimum number of monitors with data needed in a period. Default 1.

area

Column in data naming each person's area, for area-level sources. If NULL, the source's boundaries are used.

urban

Column in data flagging urban residence (for radius_km = "dhs").

name

Name of the exposure column in the output.

format

"long" (one row per person, window and radius, with coverage and window dates) or "wide" (one row per person, one column per window and radius).

Value

A data frame of class svy_exposure_result. In long format: id, window, radius_km, the exposure column, coverage, window_start and window_end.

Details

Space. For rasters, the exposure is the coverage-weighted summary of raster cells inside a circle of the chosen radius. For monitor and grid tables, monitors inside the radius are combined by assign: their "mean", the "nearest" one, or an inverse-distance weighted mean ("idw"). For area tables, the person's area value is used and the radius is ignored. Distances to monitors are great-circle distances in metres.

Time. A window is a pair c(start, end) of offsets from the anchor date, in window_unit, with both ends inclusive. c(-270, -1) in days is the 270 days before the anchor date. Months and years follow the calendar, so c(-9, 0) in months is the nine calendar months up to the anchor date. Windows may overlap and be nested, so a cumulative window is simply a long one. A day-level exposure is the mean over the days of the window; periods longer than a day (a month of a monthly raster, a year of an annual table) are weighted by how many of their days fall inside the window.

Completeness. coverage is the share of the window's days that had an exposure value. Windows below min_coverage return NA, so a window that starts before the data begin is not silently averaged over a fraction of its length.

Examples

readings <- data.frame(
  monitor = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 400),
  lon = rep(c(-0.20, -0.18), each = 400), lat = 5.6,
  date = rep(as.Date("2019-01-01") + 0:399, 2),
  pm25 = c(rep(30, 400), rep(50, 400))
)
kids <- data.frame(id = 1:2, date = as.Date(c("2019-10-01", "2019-12-15")),
                   lon = -0.195, lat = 5.6)
src <- svy_exposure(readings, unit = "monitor", value = "pm25")
svy_expose(kids, src, windows = svy_windows("prenatal_postnatal"),
           radius_km = c(1, 5), name = "pm25")
#> Warning: 2 window/radius combinations have no exposure values at all.
#> ℹ Check that the exposure data cover the window dates and the people's
#>   locations, or lower `min_coverage`.
#> <svy_exposure_result>: 2 records, 2 windows, 2 radius settings; source: points
#>     window radius_km n pct_with_value median_coverage
#>  postnatal         1 2              0            0.25
#>   prenatal         1 2            100            1.00
#>  postnatal         5 2              0            0.25
#>   prenatal         5 2            100            1.00
#> 
#>  id    window radius_km pm25  coverage window_start window_end
#>   1  prenatal         1   30 1.0000000   2019-01-04 2019-09-30
#>   2  prenatal         1   30 1.0000000   2019-03-20 2019-12-14
#>   1 postnatal         1   NA 0.3479452   2019-10-01 2020-09-29
#>   2 postnatal         1   NA 0.1424658   2019-12-15 2020-12-13
#>   1  prenatal         5   40 1.0000000   2019-01-04 2019-09-30
#>   2  prenatal         5   40 1.0000000   2019-03-20 2019-12-14
#> # ... with 2 more rows
